original_value: As wireless sensing has developed, wireless behavior recognition has become a promising research area, in which human motion duration is one of the basic and significant parameters to measure human behavior. At present, however, there is no consideration of the duration estimation of human motion leveraging wireless signals. In this paper, we propose a novel system for robust duration estimation of human motion (R-DEHM) with WiFi in the area of interest. To achieve this, we first collect channel statement information (CSI) measurements on commodity WiFi devices and extract robust features from the CSI amplitude. Then, the back propagation neural network (BPNN) algorithm is introduced for detection by seeking a cutting line of the features for different states, i.e., moving human presence and absence. Instead of directly estimating the duration of human motion, we transform the complex and continuous duration estimation problem into a simple and discrete human motion detection by segmenting the CSI sequences. Furthermore, R-DEHM is implemented and evaluated in detail. The results of our experiments show that R-DEHM achieves the human motion detection and duration estimation with the average detection rate for human motion more than 94% and the average error rate for duration estimation less than 8%, respectively.

result.paraphrase: With the growth of wireless sensing, wireless behavior recognition has emerged as a promising research field, where human motion duration is a fundamental and important parameter for measuring human behavior. However, there is currently no work considering duration estimation of human motion using wireless signals. In this paper, we propose R-DEHM, a novel system for robust duration estimation of human motion with WiFi in the area of interest. To do so, we first collect channel state information (CSI) from commodity WiFi devices and extract robust features from CSI amplitude. Then, the back propagation neural network (BPNN) algorithm is used for detection by finding a separating line in the feature space for different states, namely moving human presence and absence. Rather than estimating motion duration directly, we segment the CSI sequences and convert the complex, continuous duration estimation task into a simpler discrete human motion detection problem. In addition, R-DEHM is implemented and evaluated in detail. Experimental results show that R-DEHM achieves human motion detection and duration estimation, with an average detection rate above 94% and an average duration estimation error below 8%, respectively.
